newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army trainers charged with rape, harassment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army trainers charged with rape, harassment.

text.p: Three male Army trainers including two drill instructors have been charged in a rape and sex harassment case involving alleged attacks on women recruits at a Maryland base, the Army said on Thursday.

The three, including a captain who was a company commander, helped train hundreds of young recruits in tasks from handling ammunition to repairing trucks at Aberdeen Proving Ground near Baltimore, officials said.
The Army said Sgt. Delmar Simpson had been jailed on charges including rape, sodomy, adultery and obstruction of justice and illegal fraternisation with recruits.
Capt. Derrick Robertson, charged with rape, adultery and conduct unbecoming to an officer as well as fraternisation, has been relieved of duty pending further investigation.
Staff Sgt. Nathanial Beach has been charged with disobeying an order, obstruction of justice and fraternisation. Neither Robertson nor Beach were in custody.

Army lawyers said conviction of rape in the service is punishable by penalties that can range up to life in prison. Previously the penalty included a possible death sentence, but the U.S. Supreme Court struck down that provision.

A senior Army official, who asked not to be identified, said the case involved complaints from at least 17 women and had been under investigation since September. It began with a complaint from one female recruit, he said.
"This is the worst thing I've ever come across" in three decades in the Army, Maj. Gen. Robert Shadley, commander of the Army's Training and Doctrine Command, told reporters.
Other service officials said the case could get worse and that some 500 female recruits and former recruits had already been questioned.
Army Chief of Staff Gen. Dennis Reimer and civilian Army Secretary Togo West expressed shock and said all Army personnel would be ordered to undergo renewed sexual harassment training.

Hundreds of young men and women in their late teens and early 20s are taught skills at the Army Ordnance and Training Command facility at Aberdeen after completing eight weeks of basic training when they join the service.

"Sexual harassment is particularly repugnant when it involves abuse of authority," West said in a statement. "Drill sergeants and training personnel are the front line of the Army's professionalism and ethic -- they mould our new soldiers."

The armed forces have been plagued by a series of sexual harassment incidents despite a crackdown by the Pentagon in the wake of the 1991 "Tailhook" scandal, in which male Navy and Marine pilots harassed and fondled women at a Las Vegas hotel.
